# Page 28^page=28
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 28 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS MeitY Selects 10 Startups for Cohort II of ISG Under IndiaAI Mission In April 2026, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), announced the selection of 10 Indian Artificial Intelligence (AI) startups for the second cohort of the IndiaAI Startups Global (ISG) Acceleration Programme under the IndiaAI Mission. • The program aligns with India’s National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy which focuses on cross-border knowledge exchange, exposure to advanced entrepreneurial ecosystems and global market integration. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Selection of 10 Startups for Cohort-II of ISG Acceleration Programme ✓ Who? MeitY ✓ Mission: IndiaAI Mission ✓ Programme: IndiaAI Startups Global (ISG) Acceleration Programme ✓ Partners: Station F & HEC Paris ✓ Cohort Size: 10 startups ✓ Selected Startups: AI Health Highway India Private Limited; Awiros; Cognecto; Flaunt, among others About IndiaAI Startups Global Acceleration Programme: Part of IndiaAI Mission: The programme was initiated by the IndiaAI Mission, MeitY, under its Startup Financing Pillar. Developed by: It was developed in collaboration with Station F(France), the world’s largest startup campus and HEC Paris (France), one of Europe’s premier business schools. Cohort Support: Each cohort equips 10 selected Indian AI startups with resources, expertise, and strategic connections to scale globally. Key Sector: The second cohort of the program covers sectors like: healthtech, climate tech, edtech, satellite intelligence, and cognitive AI, as well as other categories. Programme Highlights: Selection Process: These 10 startups have been selected through a rigorous multi-stage evaluation process, representing India’s dynamic AI innovation ecosystem at Station F, for an immersive programme designed to support their global scale-up. Selected Startups: • AI Health Highway India Private Limited: It is tasked to develop an AI enabled smart stethoscope to screen, detect and predict cardio respiratory disorders; • Awiros: It will develop an AI platform enabling agentic, context-aware intelligence and automation across large-scale physical environments; • Cognecto: An AI infrastructure intelligence platform; • Flaunt: It will provide multimodal AI agents for beauty/fashion trends and short-form video marketing; • GreenFi.ai Climateforce Technologies Private Limited: It will design an AI-enabled risk management software for environment, social and governance compliance; • Infiheal Healthtech Private Limited: Healo, a multilingual AI mental health companion with human-in-loop;

# Page 29^page=29
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 29 Daily Content PDF • InLustro Learning Private Limited: It will offer AI-powered job simulation platform validating execution readiness of humans and AI agents before real-world deployment; • PredCo: AI-powered compliance for modern manufacturing across people, process and product; • SkyServe (Hyspace Technologies Private Limited): AI infrastructure for Earth & Space monitoring; • TestAIng Solutions Private Limited: A comprehensive QA and compliance suite for AI solutions ensuring trusted and responsible AI. Preparation Module: The programme includes a 3 week online preparation module followed by a three- month immersive residency in Paris, France. Key Interventions: The programme, designed by HEC Paris, will facilitate startups with unparalleled access to resources, mentorship and networking opportunities with leading French and European ecosystem players during their residency. About IndiaAI Mission: Background: In March 2024, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi approved the India AI Mission, with a budget outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years (2024–2029). Nodal Body: The mission is being implemented by the IndiaAI Independent Business Division (IBD) which works under MeitY. Compute Pillar: The Compute Pillar of IndiaAI mission offers subsidized high-end Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), scaling from 10,000 to over 38,000 GPUs at affordable access rates. Key Pillars: The mission is structured around seven key pillars that include: IndiaAI Compute Pillar, IndiaAI Application Development Initiative, AIKosh (Dataset Platform), IndiaAI Foundation Models, IndiaAI Future Skills, IndiaAI Startup Financing, Safe and Trusted AI. About Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY): Union Minister – Ashwini Vaishnaw (Rajya Sabha – Odisha) Minister of State (MoS) – Jitin Prasada (Constituency – Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, UP) AICTE Launches 3rd Edition of VAANI Scheme to Promote Indian Languages in Technical Education In April 2026, the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), under the Ministry of Education (MoE), led by Chairman Yogesh Singh, launched the third edition of the AICTE-VAANI (Vibrant Advocacy for Advancement and Nurturing of Indian Languages) scheme, in New Delhi, Delhi. • The scheme was inaugurated by Yogesh Singh, Chairman of AICTE, along with the release of the scheme document and a dedicated online application portal. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of 3rd edition of AICTE-VAANI ✓ By Whom? AICTE Chairman Yogesh Singh ✓ Duration: 2026–27 ✓ Funding: Rs 4 crore annually; Rs 2 lakh per programme ✓ Events supported: 200 conferences/seminars/workshops ✓ Focus areas: AI, Quantum Technology, Cybersecurity, Space, Hydrogen Energy ✓ Languages: 22 (Eighth Schedule).

# Page 30^page=30
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 30 Daily Content PDF Background: 1st Edition: AICTE-VAANI was launched in 2024 by T. G. Sitharam, former Chairman of AICTE, with an initial outlay of Rs.2 crore, supporting 100 academic events across 12 regional languages. 2nd Edition: In 2025, the scheme was significantly expanded, doubling its budget to Rs.4 crore, increasing coverage to 22 languages, and supporting 200 annual academic events, thereby greatly enhancing its reach and impact. Key Features of VAANI Third Edition (2026-27): Aim: The initiative aims to bridge the language gap in higher education and make advanced engineering and technical concepts accessible in regional languages, aligning with the goals of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. Funding: The scheme allocates an annual outlay of Rs.4 crore to support 200 conferences, seminars, and workshops across India, with each eligible institution receiving Rs.2 lakh per event to conduct 2–3 day academic activities. Languages: Events are conducted in 22 Indian languages listed under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. Domains: It covers 16 emerging technology areas including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Quantum Technology (QT), Cybersecurity, Hydrogen Energy, Space and Defence, and Agrotech. Application: Applications are accepted from 18 April to 17 May 2026 through the AICTE Training and Learning (ATAL) online portal. Eligibility: Institutions must be approved by AICTE, ranked in National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2024 or 2025, have at least 50% National Board of Accreditation (NBA)-accredited courses, and a National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) score of 3.01 or above 4.0. Participation: Minimum 50 participants are required, including faculty, research scholars, Master of Technology (M.Tech) students, and industry professionals, with at least one-third resource persons from industry and a senior faculty coordinator. About All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE): Chairman – Professor Yogesh Singh Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi Established – 1945 Herbalife India and IIT Madras Sign MoU to Establish India’s First COE on Plant Cell Fermentation On April 17, 2026, Herbalife India, a subsidiary of Herbalife Limited (HLF) and the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras, Chennai (Tamil Nadu, TN), signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish India’s first Centre of Excellence (CoE) on Plant Cell Fermentation Technology at IIT Madras Research Park in Chennai. Exam Hint: ✓ What? MoU signed to Establish CoE on Plant Cell Fermentation ✓ Partners: Herbalife India & IIT Madras ✓ Where? IIT Madras Research Park ✓ First in India: Dedicated CoE for plant cell fermentation ✓ Objective: Sustainable production of herbal biomass & phytochemicals ✓ Focus: Plant cell fermentation for health & wellness applications. About CoE on Plant Cell Fermentation Technology: Objective: To establish a world-class CoE for Research & Development (R&D), innovation, and entrepreneurship in the sustainable production of herbal biomass, enriched extracts, and high-value phytochemicals.

# Page 31^page=31
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 31 Daily Content PDF Focus Area: The CoE will advance plant cell fermentation for sustainable, scalable production of herbal biomass enriched with high-value phytochemicals for human health and wellness. Exam Hint: ✓ What? Empowerment: The partnership will provide MSMEs with comprehensive logistics insights, helping reduce inefficiencies, optimise costs, and enhance competitiveness in domestic and global markets. NLDSL: It is a Joint Venture (JV) between the Government of India (GoI’s) NICDIT (National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust) and the Japanese tech giant NEC Corporation. • It operates the Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) to digitise and streamline the logistics supply chain. BANKING & FINANCE RBI issues Master Directions on Notes and Coins Exchange Facility In April 2026, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) released Master Directions on Facility for Exchange of Notes and Coins, mandating all bank branches to provide free and non-discriminatory exchange services of currency notes and coins to the public. • The Directions and Guidelines were effective from April 1 2026. Exam Hints ✓ What? Master Directions on Facility for Exchange of Notes and Coins ✓ Released by: RBI ✓ Notes Accepted: Soiled, Mutilated, Imperfect, Stained ✓ Counter Exchange: No charge and counter exchange for soiled notes up to 20 pieces, maximum value Rs 5000/day ✓ Mutilated & Imperfect: Up to 10 pieces over the counter, above 10 pieces/ Rs 5000 per day account credit

# Page 32^page=32
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 32 Daily Content PDF Key Highlights Exchange Facility: RBI has instructed that all bank branches in all parts of the country are mandated to provide following customer services: • Issuing fresh/ good quality notes and coins of all denominations, • Exchanging soiled/ mutilated/ imperfect notes, and • Accepting coins and notes either for transactions or exchange. Soiled Note: A ‘soiled note’ means a note which has become dirty due to normal wear and tear and also includes a two-piece note pasted together wherein both the pieces presented belong to the same note and form the entire note with no essential feature missing. • These notes shall be accepted over bank counters for exchange or credit to accounts of the public maintained with banks. Mutilated Notes: A mutilated note is a note of which a portion is missing or which is composed of more than two pieces. • The notes presented shall be accepted, exchanged and adjudicated in accordance with Note Refund Rules (NRR), 2009 (as amended in 2018). Imperfect Notes: Imperfect note means any note, which is wholly or partially, obliterated, shrunk, washed, altered or indecipherable but does not include a mutilated note. Stained Notes: All Bank notes with scribbling/ stain (including colour/ oil stain) on them continue to be legal tender. Such notes can be deposited or exchanged in any bank branch. Notes Not Accepted: Notes which have turned extremely brittle, charred or inseparably stuck up together and, therefore, cannot withstand normal handling, shall not be accepted by the bank branches for exchange. • The holders shall be advised to present these notes to the Issue Office of RBI, where they will be adjudicated under a Special Procedure. Note: In case value of soiled/ mutilated/ imperfect notes tendered for exchange is above Rs 50,000, banks are expected to take the usual precautions. Procedure for Exchange of Soiled Notes No Charge: Where the number of notes presented by a person is up to 20 pieces with a maximum value of Rs 5,000 per day, banks shall exchange them over the counter, free of charge. Bulk Notes: Where the number of notes presented by a person exceeds 20 pieces or Rs 5,000 in value per day, banks shall accept them against receipt, for value to be credited within 7 days. • Banks may levy reasonable service charges as permitted in RBI (Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025. Procedure for Exchange of Mutilated and Imperfect Notes 10 pieces: Where the number of notes presented by a person is up to 10 pieces, bank branches shall normally adjudicate the notes and pay the exchange value over the counter. More than 10 pieces: Where the number of notes presented by a person exceeds 10 pieces or Rs 5,000 in value per day, bank branches shall accept them against receipt, for value to be credited later. Distribution of Coins Coin Acceptance: None of the bank branches shall refuse to accept coins and/ or small denomination notes tendered at their counters. • All coins in the denomination of 50 paise, Rs 1, Rs 2, Rs 5, Rs 10 and Rs 20 issued by the Government of India should be accepted. • It reiterates that coins up to Rs 20 remain legal tender, while coins of Rs.25 paise and below are no longer valid. Minimum Stock: To ensure steady supply of coins to bulk customers, all banks may ensure that each of their branches maintain a minimum stock of one bag of coins in each denomination.

Governor – Sanjay Malhotra Headquarters – Mumbai, Maharashtra DGFT Authorizes 17 Banks to Import Gold & Silver Until March 2029 In April 2026, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), under the Department of Commerce (DoC), Ministry of Commerce & Industry (MoC&I), updated the list of authorised banks, permitting 15 banks to import both gold and silver and 2 banks to import only gold. • As per DGFT, the authorisation will come into effect from April 01, 2026 and will remain valid till March 31, 2029. • The previous order, issued in April 2025, expired on 31 March 2026. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Issue of Revised List of Banks for Import of Gold & Silver ✓ Granted by: DGFT(MoCI) ✓ Total Banks: 17 including 15 (import of both gold and silver) and 2 (import of only gold) ✓ Time Period: April 01, 2026 till March 31, 2029 ✓ Banks for Gold & Silver: Axis Bank, Federal Bank, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, IndusInd Bank, KMBL, KVB, Yes Bank, Deutsche Bank, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, BoI, IOB, PNB, RBL Bank and SBI ✓ Banks for Import of Gold: UBI and SBER Bank. Key Details: Objective: The move aims to ensure efficient supply and maintain price stability in the domestic market. Key Amendment: As per DGFT official notification, this authorisation was granted through amendments made in Appendix 4 of the Handbook of Procedures, 2023 under the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP), 2023. List of Banks: The revised list includes 15 banks approved by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to import both gold and silver: • Public Sector Bank (PSBs): Indian Overseas Bank (IOB); Bank of India (BoI); Punjab National Bank (PNB); State Bank of India (SBI). • Private Banks: Axis Bank Limited; Federal Bank Limited; HDFC Bank Limited; ICICI Bank Limited; IndusInd Bank Limited; Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited (KMBL); Karur Vysya Bank Limited (KVB); Yes Bank Limited; RBL Bank Limited. • Foreign Banks: Deutsche Bank; Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited; • These banks are authorised by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to undertake bullion imports. Banks Authorized to Import Only: Apart from these banks, two banks have been authorized to import only gold: Union Bank of India (UBI) and SBER Bank, a Russian state-publicly listed company. Key Developments: Regulation: Importers outside Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and Export-Oriented Units (EOUs) must obtain specific government licences to import precious metals; the rule is effective immediately, with no transition period, including for in-transit shipments. Import Trend: India’s gold imports increased by 28.73% to USD 69 billion during April–February 2025–26, compared to the previous year, driven by higher gold prices. About Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT): Director General (DG)- Lav Agarwal Headquarters- New Delhi, Delhi Established in- 1991

# Page 34^page=34
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 34 Daily Content PDF World Bank Approves USD 225 Million Loan for Rajasthan Highway Modernization Project On April 13, 2026, the World Bank (WB’s) Board of Executive Directors approved a USD 225 million (approximately Rs. 2,080 crore) loan for the Rajasthan Highway Modernisation Project to enhance the efficiency, resilience, and safety of state highways. • This project shifts the focus from simple construction to a ‘Road as a Service’ model, emphasizing user experience and long-term asset performance. Exam Hint: ✓ What? Approved USD 225 Million Loan ✓ For: Rajasthan Highway Modernization Project ✓ Funding Agency: IBRD (World Bank) ✓ Maturity: 35 Years ✓ Significance: India’s first Step-Up Loan (SuL) ✓ Scope: ~800 km highways; institutional reform (RSHA) ✓ Key Features: Climate-resilient design, Safe Systems, Road as a Service. About Rajasthan Highway Modernisation Project: Loan Terms: The USD 225 million loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) has a 35-year maturity, includes India’s first Step-Up Loan (SuL), and offers a 5-year grace period. SuL Mechanism: The SuL eases fiscal pressure during the early high-risk phase, with higher repayments later once the project stabilises and becomes ready for market refinancing. Scope: The Rajasthan Highway Modernization Project will upgrade and maintain about 800 kilometer (km) of state highways while transforming the Rajasthan State Highway Authority (RSHA) into a modern, service-oriented agency, enhancing safety, reliability, and climate resilience. Private Investment: By mobilising nearly USD 295 million in private capital through Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) and market borrowings, the project reduces dependence on state budgets while enhancing mobility, traffic management, and lowering transportation costs. Key Objectives: • Infrastructure: Upgrade state highways into modern, climate-resilient roads, with bypasses and bridges to reduce urban congestion. • Road Safety: Deploy ATMS on 250 km of high-risk routes to enhance safety and reduce fatalities. • Economic Impact: Improve ‘good/fair’ roads from 40% to 70%, reducing travel time and boosting transport efficiency. About Rajasthan: Rajasthan, one of India’s largest states, serves as a strategic gateway connecting nearly 40% of the country’s markets. Chief Minister (CM) – Bhajan Lal Sharma Governor – Haribhau Kisanrao Bagde Capital – Jaipur Tiger Reserve (TR) – Ranthambore TR, Sariska TR CheQ and AU SFB Launch India’s First Co-branded LED Credit Card In April 2026, CheQ, a credit management platform, partnered with AU Small Finance Bank (AU SFB) to launch the ‘CheQ AU Credit Card’, India’s first co-branded Light-Emitting Diode (LED)-powered credit card, designed to simplify payments, maximise rewards, and enhance digital payment experiences through a unified rewards ecosystem and innovative tap-to-pay features. • The card lights up during transactions by drawing power from the Near Field Communication (NFC) field of the Point-of-Sale (POS) terminal, eliminating the need for an internal battery.

ECONOMY & BUSINESS JSW Steel Board Approves Proposal to Sign Pact with POSCO for JV In April 2026, JSW Steel Limited’s Board approved a proposal to form a Joint Venture (JV) with South Korea’s POSCO Group to set up a 6 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA) integrated steel plant in Odisha. • The proposed JV is expected to strengthen strategic relations between the two steel makers. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Approval to sign pact for JV steel plant ✓ Approved by: Board of JSW Steel Limited ✓ Partner: POSCO Group (South Korea) ✓ Purpose: To form JV (50:50) Between JSW and POSCO ✓ Key Highlight: To set up 6 MTPA Steel Plant in Odisha. Key Details: 50:50 JV: Both entities will sign a share subscription and JV agreement under which Saffron Resources Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of JSW Steel, will become a 50:50 JV between JSW Steel and POSCO Group through subscription arrangement.
